newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan prosecutors arrest four DKB offcials.
newsitem.headline: Japan prosecutors arrest four DKB offcials.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors said on Thursday they had arrested four officials of one of Japan's top commercial banks, Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, on suspicion of loaning 11.78 billion yen ($101 million) to a racketeer.

The loans violated Japan's Commercial Code, they said. They also said they had indicted the racketeer, Ryuichi Koike, in connection with a scandal involving payoffs of 47.49 million yen ($409,000) from Nomura Securities Co Ltd, Japan's largest brokerage.
Prosecutors said DKB made the loans through Daiwa Shinyo, a finance firm closely associated with DKB, in 51 installments from July 1994 to September 1996.
They said the loans were not properly collateralised as required by Japanese law.

Ryuichi Koike and his younger brother, Yoshinori, already in custody for suspected payoffs from Nomura, were served with fresh arrest warrants on Thursday in connection with the DKB loans, prosecutors said.

Nomura and DKB are at the centre of a widening scandal involving suspected illegal payoffs to the "sokaiya" racketeer. Sokaiya typically purchase shares in major firms and then extort money from them by threatening to disrupt shareholders' meetings.
